questions.prompt: A pension fund manages ₹40,000 crore and buys corporate bonds for its portfolio. Which side of the market is it on?
choices: Sell-side, because it is selling capital to issuers
Buy-side, because it owns securities for its own portfolio
Neither — pension funds sit outside the sell-side/buy-side split
Both, since it trades in the secondary market
questions.explanation: Buy-side. The labels describe a firm's role in the system, not the direction of any single trade: the buy-side owns securities, the sell-side manufactures and distributes them.

questions.prompt: An M&A banker learns her client will announce a takeover in three weeks. Why can she not pass this to the bank's trading desk?
choices: Trading desks are only permitted to act on research published in-house
She is on the private side holding material non-public information; trading on it is insider dealing
The information would move the price and reduce her advisory fee
Internal policy discourages it, though it is legally permitted
questions.explanation: IBD sits on the private side. Passing material non-public information across the information barrier to a desk that can trade is insider dealing — a criminal offence, not an internal preference.

questions.prompt: Which fee is earned regardless of whether a transaction completes?
choices: Asset management fees on assets under management
All three are contingent on completion
questions.explanation: Asset management charges a percentage of assets annually whether or not anything happens. M&A success fees and underwriting spreads both require a transaction to close.

questions.prompt: The information barrier between IBD and Sales & Trading exists mainly to reduce internal competition between divisions.
questions.explanation: False. It exists because IBD holds material non-public information, and letting it reach a trading desk would be insider dealing.

questions.prompt: A friend says: 'Investment banks are just brokers with better suits — they match buyers and sellers and take a cut.' Explain where this is right and where it is incomplete. Use at least two specific divisions in your answer.
rubric: Concedes the intermediation point is genuinely correct: banks do stand between capital and those who need it, and are paid for closing that gap
Identifies that a bank is several distinct businesses, not one, and names at least two divisions specifically (IBD, Sales & Trading, Research, Asset Management)
Explains that advisory work in IBD is judgment and execution over months, not order matching
Notes that Sales & Trading may commit the bank's own capital and take risk, which a pure broker does not
Mentions the information barrier or the private-side/public-side split as something a simple brokerage model does not have to manage
